findings.title: getBaseConditions returns unparenthesized top-level OR fragments that break when composed with additional AND predicates
findings.body: For org and team scopes, buildAuthorizationConditions returns a top-level OR expression (buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, lines 171-174, produces `(A) OR (B)`; buildTeamAuthorizationCondition, lines 204-207, likewise), and when there are no filters getBaseConditions returns that fragment verbatim via `return authConditions;` at line 75. The same problem exists for a lone eventTypeId filter, which is returned as `("eventTypeId" = $1) OR ("eventParentId" = $1)` without wrapping parentheses (lines 106, 119-122). The purpose of getBaseConditions() is to be embedded as the WHERE clause of larger raw queries; as soon as a caller appends `AND <predicate>` (e.g. a date-range or status filter, which insights queries typically add), SQL precedence turns `A OR B AND C` into `A OR (B AND C)`, so rows matching A are returned regardless of the appended predicate — silently wrong result sets and potentially data outside the intended filter. The OR-reduced fragments should be wrapped in parentheses before being returned.

findings.title: Public findMany() removed with no replacement query path or caller migration
findings.body: The PR deletes the service's only query-execution method, `findMany(findManyArgs)` (which merged caller-supplied where/select args with the authorization and filter conditions), and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()` returning a raw SQL fragment. No other files in the repo are changed, so any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` — the old integration test was one — will fail to compile or lose functionality. If the service is already consumed elsewhere (e.g. insights tRPC handlers), those callers must be migrated to hand-written `$queryRaw` in the same PR; if it is not consumed yet, that should be stated. Verify all callers before merging.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted while the caching logic remains in the service
findings.body: The 'Caching' describe block, which asserted that repeated calls to getAuthorizationConditions() and getFilterConditions() return the cached conditions, was removed in this PR, but the service still implements caching via cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions (insightsBooking.ts lines 49-50 and 84-95). The caching path is now untested: a regression that drops the cache would go unnoticed and would silently re-run the membership/team database lookups on every call to these methods.

findings.title: PR description misdescribes the change as a tests-only update
findings.body: The description states the PR only updates the integration tests 'to work with the new Prisma.sql format that was previously converted in the service implementation', but the diff actually performs the service conversion itself (object notation → Prisma.sql) and removes the public findMany method. A reviewer following the description could skip reviewing the new authorization SQL in the service, even though the same description flags that area as HIGH RISK. The description should be corrected to cover the service changes.
